newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Hindu party to stake claim in key state.
newsitem.headline: India's Hindu party to stake claim in key state.

text.p: India's right-wing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said on Wednesday it had agreed with an influential party of lower-caste Hindus to form a government in Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state.
The northern state has been under direct rule from New Delhi since inconclusive local elections last September failed to produce a clear majority for any one political group.

A BJP spokesman told Reuters that under Wednesday's agreement his party would allow the rival Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) to head the two-party coalition government for six months, followed by a six-month turn at the helm by the BJP.
"Every six months we will change the party to head the government," the spokesman said. "The first government will be headed by the BSP."
"Tonight we will be going to the governor to stake our claim to form the government and BSP has declared its support," BJP president Lal Krishan Advani told a news conference.
BJP has 177 members in the 425-member state assembly and the BSP 67.

The BSP's decision to join with the BJP was seen as a major setback for the Congress party, which had ruled India for all but three years since independence from Britain in 1947 and derived its strength largely from Uttar Pradesh.
The BSP and the Congress had jointly fought the September elections to the state legislature. Congress has 33 lawmakers in the legislature.
"We had asked the Congress to withdraw support to the United Front government but they did not do so, so probably they lost the opportunity," BSP chief Kanshi Ram said.
But the Congress party and Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front coalition leaders sharply criticised the pact between BJP and the BSP to forge a coalition government.
"This news does not bode well for the BSP nor for Uttar Pradesh," a Congress official told Reuters. "This kind of opportunism is going to make politicians look like saleable commodities."
But BSP chief Kanshi Ram rejected the charges. "We stand for change, BSP does not like the status quo, BSP is always in search of opportunities to improve," he said.
Sharad Yadav, working president of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's Janata Dal Party said the BJP-BSP alliance was an unholy tie up to grab power, the United News of India (UNI) reported.
The BJP-BSP pact followed protests in parliament by the BJP which has demanded the dismissal of Uttar Pradesh governor Romesh Bhandari, saying he was responsible for a jump in crime in the state.
The parliament is expected to debate the issue on Thursday.
